# Charles Jiang, MD, MPH

> Changchuan (Charles) Jiang, MD, MPH, is a medical oncologist and health services researcher in Dallas, Texas. He treats prostate, bladder, and kidney cancers and works on access to cancer care: clinical trial enrollment, supportive care, insurance benefit design, and clinical workflows and AI. He is available for advisory work, research collaboration, and speaking.

## Short bio
Changchuan (Charles) Jiang, MD, MPH, is a medical oncologist and health services researcher in Dallas, Texas. He treats prostate, bladder, and kidney cancers and holds a joint faculty appointment in medicine and public health, with clinical practice at both an NCI-designated cancer center and a county safety-net hospital. He leads a prostate cancer trial access program funded by the American Cancer Society and co-chairs the Health Access and Disparities Committee of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer (MASCC). He has published more than 80 peer-reviewed papers, in journals including Nature Reviews Clinical Oncology, JNCI, JAMA Oncology, and Annals of Internal Medicine. He trained at Soochow University (MD), Yale School of Public Health (MPH), Mount Sinai (internal medicine residency), and Roswell Park Comprehensive Cancer Center (hematology and oncology fellowship).

## What he works on
- Clinical trial access: leads a prostate cancer trial access program at a county safety-net hospital and community sites (American Cancer Society IMPACT award, PI) and directs GU clinical trial optimization for the safety-net program. Navigation and physician engagement doubled enrollment of underrepresented patients. Under an ASCO Career Development Award he studies physician and practice variation in trial enrollment nationally (205,743 patients, 1,664 physicians, 107 community practices; about 20% of physicians account for 80% of enrollments; manuscripts under review).
- Supportive care: Co-Chair of the MASCC Health Access and Disparities Committee (member since 2023, co-chair since 2025). Research on transportation barriers, financial hardship, the value of palliative care, and insurance barriers to supportive medications.
- Insurance and access: how Medicare Advantage and Part D plan design affects oncologist networks, prior authorization, drug coverage, and time to treatment.
- Clinical workflow and AI: PI of an NCCN-supported project building reflex biomarker testing and a results dashboard into the EHR for metastatic prostate cancer at a safety-net program; member of his cancer center's AI steering committee; large language model drafts of plain-language trial summaries for patients.

## Advisory and collaboration
- Clinical development and trial teams: feasibility and enrollment planning, eligibility and visit-burden review, site activation in community and safety-net settings; clinical depth in prostate, bladder, and kidney cancer.
- Medical affairs, HEOR, and market access: real-world evidence design and interpretation, Medicare Advantage and Part D, utilization management, patient access barriers.
- Health technology and AI teams: clinical use-case review, workflow fit, evaluation design.
- Also open to research collaborations, advisory boards, grand rounds, and CME.
- Contact: LinkedIn message (https://www.linkedin.com/in/changchuan-charles-jiang-54787080/).

## Quick facts
- More than 2,500 citations and 80 peer-reviewed papers; h-index 19 (Google Scholar, September 2026)
- $1.09M in active grants as principal investigator; 50+ multicenter trials as site PI or co-investigator
- Honors: Clinical Trial Diversity Champion award (2025); Prostate Cancer Foundation Thought Leaders of the Future (2023); five ASCO Conquer Cancer Merit Awards
- Co-founder, ANACP Mentoring Program; Vice President, Research Subcommittee, ASCO IMG Community of Practice

## Affiliation and disclaimer
Assistant Professor of Internal Medicine and Public Health, UT Southwestern Medical Center. Affiliations are listed for identification only. Views on this site are his own and do not represent his employer or any affiliated institution. Advisory work is done in a personal capacity and disclosed under institutional conflict-of-interest policies.
